adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the object shape uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to plain strings (likely the same default `"[object Object]"`), meaning they become fixed literal property names in the schema, not “any string key”. In a JS object literal, duplicate keys overwrite, so one definition can replace the other. As a result, the intended validation (“any numeric property is the expiry, and allow other properties”) does not work; it either requires a bizarre literal key or loses the numeric-key rule entirely, effectively removing expiry validation under the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` path.
